2  The non-LTE spectrum of the TITAN quasi-star

Modified

October 18, 2026

2.1 The model

The star. A 10^6\,M_\odot quasi-star with a 10^5\,M_\odot black hole, from the stellar-structure models of Santarelli et al. (2026): radius R = 8.4352\times10^{15} cm and luminosity L_0 = 1.420\times10^{44} erg s^{-1}. TITAN, ported to Julia, evolves its envelope in radiation hydrodynamics on an adaptive grid. It uses zero-metallicity LTE opacities, without lines, and mixing-length convection (details in the detailed book).

The infall. In run W30, gas enters through an outer boundary at 30R at 3\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1} and the free-fall speed. It reaches the star at v_{\rm ff}(R) = 1770 km s^{-1} and stops in a radiative shock at the photosphere. Behind the shock a thin cooling layer reaches 3.7\times10^7 K and radiates the kinetic power \tfrac12\dot M v^2 = 2.6\times10^{42} erg s^{-1}, 2 % of L_0, mostly as hard free–free emission. The star settles after a few dynamical times. From 2\times10^8 s to 4.5\times10^8 s its photosphere stays at r_{\rm ph} = 0.989R, T_{\rm eff} = 7310 \pm 17 K and L = 0.997\,L_0 [computed]. Moving the outer boundary from 1.2R to 30R changes none of this.

The spectrum calculation. It uses the snapshot at 4.18\times10^8 s.

  • Continuum: static spherical transfer through the star, the shock layer and the infall, out to 120R. Beyond TITAN’s 30R we assume the same free fall continues, with T \propto r^{-1/2}. It includes coherent Thomson scattering, and the temperatures below the shock are corrected to radiative equilibrium for the non-grey opacities (Unsöld–Lucy).
  • Hydrogen out of LTE: wherever the infall is cooler than 2\times10^4 K (118 points from just above the shock to 120R). The atom has twelve levels plus the proton. Collision rates are approximate, and line transfer uses Sobolev escape probabilities in the free-fall velocity field.
  • Coupling: the bound–free rates use the mean intensity from the full transfer, which in turn uses the non-LTE opacities and emissivities, iterated to convergence. X-rays above 100 eV make secondary ionizations.
  • Held fixed: TITAN’s temperatures and densities. Helium stays in LTE.

The iteration took 140 passes. Over the last 40, without acceleration, the ionized fraction moved by at most 0.016 and n_2 by at most 3.7 % [computed].

2.2 The infall is ionized by the star

Hydrogen is more than 99 % ionized out to 4.2R, 92 % at 8.5R, 50 % at 40R and 8 % at 120R [computed]. In LTE at the same temperatures it would be neutral beyond 2R (Chapter 3).

  • The neutral column is 8.5\times10^{23} cm^{-2} out of 9.0\times10^{24} cm^{-2} in all.
  • The infall has a Thomson depth of 5.4: an electron-scattering cocoon around the star.
  • The collision rates (×0.3, ×3), the X-rays (switched off) and the Lyman-continuum treatment were varied on the earlier run A220. None of them changes the neutral column by more than 10 % [tested].

What does ionize it is worked out in Chapter 4: the star’s far-UV light pumps the Lyman lines, and the excited atoms are photoionized by its optical light.

2.3 Hα in strong emission

The Hα source function is above the local continuum everywhere in the infall (apart from a thin X-ray-heated layer just above the shock, below 0.9913R). S_L/J_c = 1.4 just above the star, 11 at 4.7R, 32 at 13R and about 60 at 30R. The line is optically thick: Sobolev depths range from 10 to 2800 [computed].

The profiles are integrated along rays through the infall with the non-LTE populations [computed].

  • Narrow. Most of the line forms far out, where the gas falls slowly. 79 % of the line power comes from beyond 5R, 51 % from beyond 12R and 17 % from beyond 30R [computed]. The free-fall speed is 560 km s^{-1} at 10R and 280 km s^{-1} at 40R.
  • Asymmetric. The red wing reaches the infall speed at the shock. That gas falls away from us in front of the star. Gas behind the star is hidden, so the blue wing is shorter [interpretation].
  • Redshifted absorption in Hβ is the infall in front of the star, absorbing its light. Hα has none because its source function is above the continuum everywhere [interpretation].

2.4 Energy

The continuum carries 1.231\times10^{44} erg s^{-1}. The hydrogen lines carry 1.1\times10^{43} erg s^{-1} in the solution’s own line balance, or 1.65\times10^{43} erg s^{-1} summed over the 23 computed emergent profiles. The difference is discussed in Section 5.3. Together this is 0.92 of TITAN’s luminosity [computed]. The power in the lines is starlight, absorbed in the Balmer and Paschen continua and re-emitted. The accretion shock adds only 2 % of L.

The missing 8 % is absorbed by infall gas whose temperature is held fixed. In reality it would heat that gas, and the temperatures would have to be solved for together with the populations. That is the main approximation left in the calculation [interpretation].

TITAN’s infall or an assumed one

The same calculation on the earlier run A220 stopped TITAN’s grid at 1.2R and assumed the free fall beyond it. W30 replaces the assumption out to 30R with TITAN’s own infall. The gas there is up to 20 % warmer than assumed at 3–4 R, but every result above moves by no more than the iteration drift. The ionized fraction at 40R is 0.51 for A220 and 0.50 for W30, Hα has EW −795 and −805 Å, and the Balmer decrement is 5.07 and 5.28 [computed]. What is still assumed is the gas beyond 30R. It emits about 17 % of the line power and holds about two thirds of the neutral column.

Santarelli, Andrew D., Claire B. Campbell, Ebraheem Farag, Earl P. Bellinger, Priyamvada Natarajan, and Matthew E. Caplan. 2026. “MESA-QUEST: Tracing the Formation of Direct Collapse Black Hole Seeds via Quasi-Stars.” The Astrophysical Journal 998: 150. https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-4357/ae371e.
